items.name: Microsoft is winding down 2023 Oracle deal to rent AI cloud capacity (Bloomberg, via Reuters)
items.headline: Microsoft is winding down 2023 Oracle deal to rent AI cloud capacity (Bloomberg, via Reuters)
items.source: Reuters on Investing.com, relaying Bloomberg; read by WebFetch
items.candidate_dial: capex deferral / digestion (principal: MSFT; counterparty ORCL)
items.claim: Bloomberg, citing people familiar, reported that Microsoft declined to renew a multi-year 2023 arrangement to rent AI computing from Oracle (used for AI-assisted Bing) and has been switching the capacity off in recent months, as part of a broader review of cloud partnerships; the hardware uses an older Nvidia chip generation. Financial terms of the deal were never disclosed. Oracle said demand for OCI AI infrastructure remains strong, including for earlier-generation GPUs.
items.sweep_query: 3. capex cut OR deferral OR digestion AI
items.note: A lease non-renewal, not a stated capex-guidance cut. No dollar or MW size given. Reuters said ORCL and MSFT were flat in afternoon trade; other syndications say Oracle fell about 3-4% (conflict not resolved). Bloomberg original not fetched. Distinct from the prior-recorded Nscale option decline (11-05) and neocloud story (11-05).

items.name: JPMorgan cuts IREN target to $55 from $65 on capex reduction and delays; remaining FY2027 capex $15bn vs $25-30bn expected
items.headline: JPMorgan cuts IREN target to $55 from $65 on capex reduction and delays; remaining FY2027 capex $15bn vs $25-30bn expected
items.source: Investing.com analyst-ratings article; read by WebFetch
items.claim: JPMorgan cut its IREN price target to $55 from $65 (Overweight kept) after IREN guided to $15bn of capex for the remainder of fiscal 2027 against a previously expected $25-30bn, attributed to a changing financing environment in which IREN is pulling back early site-development spend, plus a longer timeline for air-cooled Childress capacity. Of the $15bn, $9bn is secured and $6bn unfunded. Horizon 2-4 deliveries for Microsoft slip one month to end-January 2027, possibly February.
items.sweep_query: 3. capex cut OR deferral OR digestion AI
items.note: Underlying guidance comes from IREN's Q1 FY2027 results dated 2026-11-05; the prior list recorded the Horizon slip from those results but not the capex reduction, so this is the new element (the analyst note is dated 11-09). The article's own arithmetic is inconsistent (it calls $15bn '$7.5bn lower' than $25-30bn); the 456X Nov 7 brief instead describes full-year guidance falling from $25-30bn to $20bn with $15bn over the next three quarters. Numbers recorded as stated, not reconciled.

items.name: Reuters: Banks, investors grow wary of AI debt after selloff; some data-center and chip bond deals shelved, Nebius did not proceed with high-yield bond
items.headline: Reuters: Banks, investors grow wary of AI debt after selloff; some data-center and chip bond deals shelved, Nebius did not proceed with high-yield bond
items.source: Reuters, republished by Global Banking & Finance Review; read by WebFetch
items.claim: Reuters reports that some planned bond offerings tied to data centers and chips are being shelved and that some lenders are reluctant to finance deals even when backed by Anthropic or Google. Nebius explored a high-yield bond in September but did not go ahead in October, per one source; it instead entered a $3.5bn senior secured loan from Citigroup in October. Spreads on 10-year hyperscaler debt have widened about 50bp year to date versus about 20bp for high-quality non-AI industrials (BofA); Meta and SpaceX bonds trade below par.
items.note: The shelved deals are unnamed; the only named abandoned deal (Nebius HY bond) dates to October, outside the gate. No hyperscaler (MSFT/GOOGL/META/AMZN/ORCL) deal is reported pulled. A related FourWeekMBA page ('Some Lenders Said to Balk at AI Debt, Even With Backstops') could not be fetched.

items.name: OpenAI reportedly raises $11bn so far at $1.25tn valuation; round could total about $20bn vs $30bn at $1.4tn sought
items.headline: OpenAI reportedly raises $11bn so far at $1.25tn valuation; round could total about $20bn vs $30bn at $1.4tn sought
items.source: TechCrunch, relaying Bloomberg; read by WebFetch
items.claim: Bloomberg, citing people familiar, reported OpenAI has raised $11bn so far in a round valuing it at $1.25tn; the round is expected to close in coming weeks and could total about $20bn. In late September Bloomberg had reported OpenAI was seeking $30bn at $1.4tn, so the figures fall well short of that target.
items.note: Follow-on to the prior-recorded 10-31 item (target cut to ~$20bn at $1.25tn). The new dated development is the $11bn first tranche actually raised at the lower valuation. Investors not named in this copy; OpenAI had not commented.

items.name: Anthropic IPO: prospective buyers discuss $1.2-1.3tn valuation, some as low as $1.1tn (Bloomberg, via secondary summaries)
items.headline: Anthropic IPO: prospective buyers discuss $1.2-1.3tn valuation, some as low as $1.1tn (Bloomberg, via secondary summaries)
items.source: RoboForex blog (dated 2026-11-09) and Tech Insider (2026-11-08), both summarizing a Bloomberg report of 2026-11-06; read by WebFetch
items.claim: On 6 November Bloomberg reported that potential buyers of the Anthropic IPO were discussing a valuation of $1.2-1.3tn, with some weighing as low as $1.1tn, versus about $1.5tn reported in mid-October and about $2tn in September. No final decision has been made; formal marketing could begin the following week, and investors would reportedly accept a delay if market pressure persists.
items.note: Secondary summaries only; Bloomberg original not read, and the Quartz copy (qz.com) failed to fetch. Continues the prior-recorded sequence ($1.5tn on 11-03; WSJ 'toward $1tn' on 11-05); recorded because it is a new dated range from a different outlet. Raise size not confirmed (up to $100bn per a September Reuters report). No price range filed.

items.name: Norway reins in data centres: Statnett halts new grid-connection reservations pending licensing scheme (Reuters)
items.headline: Norway reins in data centres: Statnett halts new grid-connection reservations pending licensing scheme (Reuters)
items.source: Reuters, republished by Cyprus Mail; read by WebFetch
items.claim: Norway's government announced it will curb data-centre growth, and grid operator Statnett temporarily halted reservations of connections for new data centres until a government licensing scheme is in place. Statnett has received connection applications for 26,000 MW so far this year, more than Norway's current capacity, with data centres 75% of the requests. The planned scheme would restrict land and power access for global cloud companies and crypto firms and make new data centres pay for grid costs.
items.note: No fixed end date for the pause; no named project cancelled. Applies to new reservations, not existing allocations.

items.name: 456X Evening Brief Nov 7: ~11 GW of planned US data centers could face construction pauses; Meta and Microsoft weigh building abroad (undated estimates)
items.headline: 456X Evening Brief Nov 7: ~11 GW of planned US data centers could face construction pauses; Meta and Microsoft weigh building abroad (undated estimates)
items.source: 456X / 404K Research Substack evening brief; read by WebFetch
items.candidate_dial: GW deferral (US pipeline; principals META, MSFT mentioned)
items.claim: The brief cites unnamed estimates that about 11 GW of planned US data centers could face construction pauses, narrowing to a net domestic reduction of about 3 GW by 2030 if developers relocate; it says facilities targeting 2028-2029 energization face severe slippage or cancellation risk, and that Meta is evaluating construction outside the US and Microsoft is considering international expansion. It also cites a J.P. Morgan figure that about 78% of the high-yield data-center development pipeline is in Texas, with lease covenants allowing only 120-180 days of delivery delay.
items.note: Secondary aggregator; underlying sources unnamed and undated, so the as_of is the brief's date. Estimates of exposure, not announced deferrals. Meta 'look abroad' overlaps the prior-recorded WSJ item of 11-05. The same brief reports no memory LTA renegotiation.

items.name: Austrian property funds limit redemptions as investors seek cash (Bloomberg): Real Invest and Erste Immobilienfonds
items.headline: Austrian property funds limit redemptions as investors seek cash (Bloomberg): Real Invest and Erste Immobilienfonds
items.source: Briefs Finance summary of a Bloomberg report dated 2026-11-07; read by WebFetch (Bloomberg original refused: robots)
items.claim: Austria's two largest retail property funds, Bank Austria's Real Invest (about EUR 2.4bn, UniCredit) and Erste Immobilienfonds (about EUR 1.3bn, roughly 45% German assets), limited withdrawals last month and will speed up property sales; Erste's chief risk officer said redemptions remain high with no signs of a decline. DWS Grundbesitz Europe also capped withdrawals last month.
items.note: The limits were introduced in October 2026 (before the gate); the in-gate element is the 11-07 report and the statement that redemption pressure persists. Cap percentages not given. Read through a summary, not the Bloomberg original. Not private credit.
